To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Paracrine ATP/adenosinergic signaling contributes to the progression to fibrosis and impaired function in a murine model of PKP2 deficiency.

1) PKP2 deficiency is associated with increased ATP release in cardiomyocytes; 2) ATP release is mediated through connexin channels; 3) PKP2-deficient animals have a cardiomyopathy with fibrosis, and this is associated with increased activation of adenosinergic signaling; 4) blocking the adenosine 3 receptor mitigates the cardiomyopathy in PKP2-deficiency, whereas blocking the 2B receptor has opposite effects.
PKP2 deficiency in mice is associated with increased expression of genes involved in the adenosine 3'5'-cyclic monophosphate (cAMP) signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ATP release into the cardiac intercellular space and the subsequent activation of adenosinergic receptors in the progression of fibrofatty cardiopathy.
the role of paracrine adenosinergic signaling in the progression of fibrofatty cardiomiopathy in a PKP2-deficient mouse model.
the role of ATP release in a PKP2-related cardiomyopathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenosine 1A/2A receptor activation is a mechanism by which the loss of PKP-2 expression contributes to the progression from a cardiomyopathy to a cardiomyopathic phenotype.
the blockade of adenosine 1A receptors may mitigate the progression of the cardiomyopathy associated with loss of PKP expression.
the role of adenosine signaling in the progression of cardiomyopathies associated with PKP2 mutations needs to be further investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PKP2 loss of function leads to increased ATP release and activation of adenylyl cyclase.
the blockade of the adenosine 3A receptor may be an effective treatment in the case of PKP2 deficiency.

PKP2 loss results in increased ATP release from the cell, and that this increase in ATP is associated with an increase in adenosine receptor signaling, which in turn promotes fibrosis and mechanical dysfunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adenosine pathway is a potential target for pharmacological intervention in the treatment of PKP2-related cardiomyopathies.
adenosine 3 receptors are likely involved in the progression of fibrofatty cardiopulmonary in the case of PKP2 deficiency.
the PKP2-dependent release of ATP is a likely mechanism for the progression of cardiomyopathy in this model.
